editorial:
If you love gritty prison fight movies, this one is a blast. Boyka, once the most feared fighter in his prison, is now broken and stuck cleaning toilets after a brutal knee injury. When an international tournament offers freedom to the winner, he has to claw his way back into shape and earn his spot. The story is simple but effective, and it gives you a real reason to root for him. The fights are fast, brutal, and well choreographed, with a strong underdog vibe that keeps you hooked from start to finish.

The acting is solid for this kind of movie, especially from Scott Adkins, who makes Boyka feel tough but human. The pacing rarely slows down, and the international fighters add variety and stakes. On the downside, the plot is pretty predictable, and some side characters feel thin. Still, if you want hard-hitting action with a comeback story, this delivers. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: Boyka fights his way through the tournament and faces the final opponent in a brutal last match. Despite his injured knee and the odds against him, he refuses to quit and wins the fight. As the champion, he earns his freedom and walks out of prison, finally reclaiming his dignity and proving he is still the best fighter.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves martial arts action and comeback stories.
